question: Where is the CRC-16 of a DVD-Audio (FBB) major sync, and is it the FBA one?
method: For each stream, take the 64 bytes after the first access-unit header and test every offset k in 16..40: does CRC16_MAJOR_SYNC (oadec-bits; generator 0x002D, register 0) over bytes[0..k] equal the big-endian word at k? The same test on an FBA stream is the control.

streams.name: God Save The Queen.mlp
streams.encoder: Meridian MLP encoder 1.23 (its log is published beside the file)

reading: An FBB major sync is 28 bytes: 26 bytes of information and the CRC-16 of the FBA major sync over them, stored big-endian. No other offset matches, so the length is not a coincidence of one file. MajorSync::fbb_crc_ok tests exactly this, which is what lets the extractor tell a DVD-Audio stream from the four sync bytes met by chance in damaged data.
